seo_desc: 2 Christmas events for kids in Kenmore, WA, 2 free: Kenmore Winterfest and Argosy Christmas Ship at Log Boom Park and more.
lede: Kenmore keeps Christmas small town and lakeside, with a free Winterfest at City Hall and a beach bonfire at Log Boom Park when the Christmas Ship sails up Lake Washington.
celebrates: The City of Kenmore, which says it provides free, community focused events, hosts Winterfest each December at City Hall and the Hangar across the street, with school choirs, the Dickens Carolers, food trucks, a holiday craft market and a food drive for the Northshore Senior Center. When the Argosy Christmas Ship visits the north end of Lake Washington, the city lights a bonfire at Log Boom Park and hands out free hot cocoa. The Kenmore Heritage Society has offered free Santa photos at Kenmore Camera, and the city runs a holiday food and toy drive.
lastyear: In 2025 Kenmore's holiday calendar was full. The Argosy Christmas Ship stopped at Log Boom Park on November 30, and Winterfest filled City Hall and the Hangar on December 6 from 11 am to 3 pm. That same afternoon the Kenmore Heritage Society hosted free Santa Photos and a Winter Wonderland at Kenmore Camera from 2 to 5 pm, first come, first served. The city also ran a holiday food and toy drive and a free digital shop local pass.
facts: Kenmore was named on January 10, 1901, by mill owner John McMaster, after his old home of Kenmore, Ontario, about 40 miles south of Ottawa. His shingle mill sat at the edge of Lake Washington, where logs floated in to become roof shingles, and it burned in 1923. Kenmore Air, now one of the largest seaplane operations, began here in 1946 with one floatplane and a garage on the site of an old shingle mill. Kenmore incorporated on August 31, 1998.
trains: Railroad tracks once ran along Kenmore's lakeshore, just behind the McMaster Shingle Mill in a 1909 photo. That rail line is now the Burke Gilman Trail, whose first 12.1 miles were dedicated on August 19, 1978, from Gas Works Park in Seattle to Kenmore's Tracy Owen Station, the same spot as Log Boom Park. Sound Transit's Stride S3 bus rapid transit line will add three Kenmore stations along Bothell Way. For real train rides, families drive to the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie.

kidfact: Kenmore is named after a town in Canada. A mill owner named John McMaster came from Kenmore, Ontario, and gave his new home the same name in 1901.
faq: Kenmore Winterfest is the City of Kenmore's free December festival at City Hall, 18120 68th Avenue NE, and the Hangar across the street. It brings local school choirs and bands, the Dickens Carolers, food trucks, a holiday craft market and a food drive for the Northshore Senior Center. The city says its special events are free and community focused.
Does the Christmas Ship stop in Kenmore?

Yes. The Argosy Christmas Ship visits Log Boom Park, also called Tracy Owen Station, at the north end of Lake Washington. The City of Kenmore lights a bonfire in the beach fire pit, serves free hot cocoa and offers free parking, and the ship's choir sings carols from the water for about twenty minutes.
Where can kids get free Santa photos in Kenmore?

In recent years the Kenmore Heritage Society has hosted free Santa Photos and a Winter Wonderland at Kenmore Camera on the afternoon of Winterfest, first come, first served with no reservations. Check the society's website for the current year's date, since this year's details had not been posted when we last looked.
How did Kenmore get its name?

Mill owner John McMaster named the village on January 10, 1901, after his former home of Kenmore, Ontario, a small town about 40 miles south of Ottawa. McMaster ran a shingle mill on the Lake Washington shore. Kenmore became a city much later, on August 31, 1998, and was then the newest city in King County.
